othermeta.name: shortdesc

othermeta.content: define the purpose of manually initiating Machine Server backups
othermeta.name: usecase

ol.li: This document describes how to manually start a backup of a Machine Server. This procedure is useful after installing a new version of software, configuring new backup or primary machine servers, or whenever it is desired to ensure that the backup machine server is up to date. Normal backups of the Machine Server are scheduled to occur at 1 AM in the morning (local time).
This procedure only applies to Machine Servers which are using SWSet 223 (SCS-0237 GR-223) or later.

reference.title: Procedure

othermeta.content: Procedure: Manually Triggering a Machine Server Backup
othermeta.name: title

othermeta.content: Step-by-step procedure to manually start a Machine Server backup, verify completion, and validate data synchronization between primary and backup servers.
othermeta.name: shortdesc

othermeta.content: manually start and verify a Machine Server backup to ensure synchronized backups and readiness after changes
othermeta.name: usecase

ol.li: Log off the obop account (using the sequence Start-, andgt;Shutdown-, andgt;Log Off).
Log onto the Machine Server with the administrator account (password: scsgolden).

Trigger the scheduled tasks.
This step is for Windows Server 2003 systems only. If using Windows Server 2008 (SCS-0716 GR04 or greater), use step 4 instead.
Navigate to the Control Panel (Start -, andgt; Settings -, andgt; Control Panel or see Figure 1 below). Figure 1: Navigating to the Control Panel (Windows Server 2003 Systems)
Locate the Scheduled Tasks control and double-click it (see Figure 2). Figure 2: Scheduled Tasks Control (Windows Server 2003)
The scheduled tasks will now be displayed. Right-click each of the following scheduled tasks (in order), and then select Run:
DBBackup.
DBMonitorBackup.
BackupFiles
Wait for the system to stop displaying the message “Running” prior to moving onto the next one. (See Figure 3 for an example of a running scheduled task).
Figure 3: Scheduled Tasks Window
(Note that the DBBackup Task is Currently Running)
When the BackupFiles scheduled task is complete, the backup will have been copied to the backup server.

Trigger the scheduled tasks. This step is for Windows Server 2008 systems only. If using Windows Server 2003 (SCS-0716 GR03 or prior), use step 3 instead.
Open the Server Manager by clicking on the Start Menu, then right-clicking the Computer icon, and then selecting Manage (see Figure 4). Figure 4: Opening Server Manager (Windows Server 2008)
When Server Manager opens, navigate to the task scheduler library as shown in Figure 5. Figure 5: Scheduled Tasks (WindowsServer 2008) DBBackup Running
The scheduled tasks will now be displayed. Right-click each of the following scheduled tasks (in order) and then select “Run.”
DBBackup
DBMonitorBackup
BackupFiles
Wait for the system to stop displaying the message “ Running” prior to moving onto the next task. With Windows Server 2008, the task status does not automatically refresh, and the F5 key must be pressed to refresh the task status.
See Figure 5 for an example of a running scheduled task
When the BackupFiles scheduled task is complete, the backup will have been copied to the backup server.
Follow the instructions in FES-03-117 Verifying Machine Server Backups to validate that the backup worked correctly
